review_notes: This file has nothing the simp-interface rubric can apply to. I read all 40 lines. The file contains one declaration, `ArExplicit.ExternalTensor.map_quasiIso` (lines 14–35). Its conclusion is the typeclass proposition `QuasiIso (mapBifunctorMap f g (bifunctor k A B) (ComplexShape.down ℕ))`. That is not an equation or an iff, so it cannot serve as a rewrite rule, and there is no orientation, normal form or simp attribute to judge. The file has no `@[simp]` attributes, no `simp` calls and no other equational or iff lemmas. Its only rewrite is `rw [← h]` at line 30. Here `h` is `scalarForgetTotalIso_naturality`, which is declared in a different file (ExternalTensorForget.lean, line 163), so its orientation and simp status belong to that file's review. Inside this proof, the reverse rewrite turns `iso.hom ≫ Φ.map (...)` back into `t ≫ iso'.hom`, so that `infer_instance` can find the `QuasiIso` instance. That is a single targeted use, not a sign of a misoriented canonical rule. Whether `map_quasiIso` should be an `instance` is a question about the typeclass interface, not about simp, so I did not report it.
